title: Sliding window config leak - personal debug notes
content:
Context:
- Small but persistent throughput regression observed starting ~2024-10-19 03:00 UTC on canary cluster (region-us-west2-canary).
- Symptoms: steady drop in tokens/sec (~18-30%), p95 token latency increased from ~120ms to 240-320ms for short requests (seq_len < 64). P50 increases only slightly.
- Affected service: continuous-batcher (the persistent batching service in serving-runtime). No obvious error-level logs.

Quick hypothesis summary (working):
1) Timer/flush drift: flush interval drifting longer -> batches waiting longer -> KV cache warmup mismatch -> fewer cache hits -> increased compute per request -> throughput drop.
2) Window size misconfiguration introduced in recent PR (see PR 1423) where sliding_window_ms default changed from 50 -> 200 under certain feature-flag combos.
3) Backpressure loop: increased internal queue depth triggers backpressure signals that cascade and reduce batch creation frequency.
4) GC pauses or thread contention on vcpu pinned threads (less likely: no GC spikes in host metrics).

Commands and telemetry I ran (timestamps included):
- kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/continuous-batcher-canary --since=2h | grep -E "flush|window|queued|drift" -A3 -B1
  -> repeated lines: "WARN continuous-batcher: flush_timer drift=430ms target=50ms" around 03:04, 03:16, 03:48 (matches regression onset).

- curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":16}' -w '
%{time_total}
' -o /dev/null
  -> baseline (10/18): 0.078s, observed (10/19): 0.12-0.22s (unstable).

- kubectl exec -it pod/continuous-batcher-canary -- sh -c 'cat /etc/serving/runtime-config.yaml'
  -> saw value: batching:
       sliding_window_ms: 200
       max_batch_tokens: 10240
       max_batch_size: 32
       flush_after_ms: 5
  (note: flush_after_ms=5 but sliding_window_ms=200 is a mismatch we didn't expect)

- ps aux | grep continuous-batcher -> no obvious OOMs, CPU steady ~40%.

- curl to /metrics (prom):
  - continuous_batcher_queue_depth histogram: median shifted +3, p99 from 18 -> 46.
  - batch_creation_rate: down ~24%.
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio at model-proxy layer: fell from 0.86 -> 0.65.

Error/log snippets (copied raw):
- [2024-10-19T03:04:12.673Z] WARN continuous-batcher flush_timer drift=430ms target=50ms node=cb-7c9f9
- [2024-10-19T03:04:12.675Z] INFO batch-assembler new-batch id=0x7f2 size_tokens=512 window_ms=200 queued=14
- [2024-10-19T03:04:12.690Z] DEBUG kv-cache miss key=ctx:usr:abcd

Notes about the config mismatch:
- Previously sliding_window_ms was 50 and flush_after_ms 5. That combination gave frequent small-ish batches but good KV reuse.
- New default (from PR 1423) when feature_flag X on: sliding_window_ms bumped to 200 to favor higher throughput with larger models. But for our short-seq low-latency workloads this increases cold-kv windows.
- I suspect the code only sets sliding_window_ms per-worker on start and doesn't adapt when instance load changes (no adaptive windowing).

Experiments run (chronological):
1) 2024-10-19 06:20 UTC: restart canary pod (kube deployment restart) -> temporary throughput bump (tokens/sec +12%) for ~7 minutes then regressed back. Means not purely transient CPU/Ghost.
2) 2024-10-19 07:10 UTC: applied runtime override via k8s ConfigMap (sliding_window_ms -> 50) and rolled out on canary (1 pod)
   - outcome: tokens/sec returned to baseline within 90s, kv_cache_hit_ratio recovered to 0.84, p95 latency down to ~130ms.
   - implication: configuration change appears root-cause correlated.
3) 2024-10-19 09:00 UTC: rolled change to blue pool (10% traffic) -> partial recovery but slower (due to mixed window sizes across pool causing interference).
4) 2024-10-19 11:00 UTC: A/B test with sliding_window_ms=100 shows 8-12% recovery vs 50 baseline but still worse than 50.

Why sliding_window_ms=200 hurt throughput for short seq workloads:
- Larger window allows more requests to be grouped but increases the TTL of opportunistic KV cache entries. If entries aren't reused frequently (short prompts), the effective cache "warm" window is diluted. Result: more cache misses overall when requests have smaller context overlap.
- Larger windows also increase batch formation latency for small flows; even if flush_after_ms=5 triggers a flush, we observed internal coordination delays (flush_timer drift) leading to extra wait.

Investigation of flush_timer drift:
- Host kernel clock skew negligible.
- Observed repeated log WARN with drift ~400-500ms; root cause might be event loop starvation: an expensive periodic task (metrics export or snapshot) runs every N ms and preempts the flush loop.
- Check list of periodic tasks in batcher: snapshot_state(200ms), metrics_flush(500ms), kv_prefetch_heuristic(100s). snapshot_state runs under a lock (snapped) and takes up to 120ms at times (profiled). If snapshot_state is scheduled at same tick as flush_timer, we see effective drift.

Profiling notes (local flamegraphs):
- pprof CPU: % of time in snapshot_state ~18% under load spike; in batch_assembler ~36%; garbage collection cycles are low.
- thread contention on snapshot_state mutex: wait time spikes ~70ms in worst traces.

Recent code areas to inspect (pointers):
- pkg/batching/assembler.go: assembleWindow() around line ~412 (see TODO: optimize timer wakeup).
- pkg/telemetry/snapshot.go: snapshotState() heavy serialization path. (PR 1399 touched this area).
- PR 1423 (sliding window default change) and its feature-flag gating.

Immediate mitigations applied and outcome:
- Reverted sliding_window_ms to 50 on canary -> positive.
- Added jitter to snapshot_state scheduling in a hotfix (reduce collision chance). Observed decreased flush_timer drift WARN occurrences by ~70% in 24h.
- Added Prometheus alert: continuous_batcher_flush_drift_count > 10 in 5m.

Longer-term fixes (proposal):
1) Adaptive windowing for continuous-batcher: tune sliding_window_ms based on observed avg seq_len and kv_cache_hit_rate.
2) Move heavy snapshot serialization off the main event loop (background writer with lock-free copy).
3) Add unit/regression test simulating short-seq high-concurrency traffic verifying p95 latency doesn't regress when sliding_window_ms default changes.
4) Document default heuristics and add safe-default matrix for workload profiles (low-latency short seq vs high-throughput long seq).

Open questions / TODOs (for myself and team):
- [ ] Confirm whether feature-flag X was rolled to all clusters on 2024-10-18 (ops audit). (linked JIRA INF-2971)
- [ ] Instrument per-batch cache hit telemetry to see exact misreuse patterns by seq_len buckets.
- [ ] Run an offline sim harness that replays our short-seq traffic with different sliding_window_ms settings.
- [ ] Review PR 1399 changes to snapshot serialization with Tomás.
- [ ] Add an e2e smoke that toggles sliding_window_ms and ensures no >10% throughput regression for short-seq profile within 5m.

Notes for handoff:
- If you are debugging: check continuous-batcher logs for flush_timer drift WARN; check /metrics kv_cache_hit_ratio and batch_creation_rate; check runtime-config for sliding_window_ms.
- Quick rollback command I used:
  kubectl -n runtime set configmap runtime-config --from-file=runtime-config.yaml=./runtime-config.yaml && kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher-canary

Final personal take: this felt like a config+timing interaction more than pure algorithmic regression. The sliding_window default bump (PR 1423) was well-intentioned for long-seq throughput, but we need a safer opt-in or adaptive behavior.

Raw snippets saved here for future: 
- diff of runtime-config (before/after) and exact logs copied to /tmp/scratch/cbatch-20241019-logs.tar.gz

End of notes.
